_comment: Level 2 ground truth: claim-to-ruling mappings verified against real transcripts, per tests/model_bench/README.md's methodology (1: open the conversation + matching DECISIONS.md entries, 2: quote the claim + literal substring + ruling number, 3: record who/when, 4: start small). This consolidates every item verified so far -- the original 3-item seed (minus one item superseded by richer coverage below) plus every timeline event logged in tests/model_bench/synthesis_case_studies/*.json, reshaped into a flat, scoreable list.
schema_note: Each item is one claim a candidate model's K2 extraction on `conversation_id` SHOULD be able to surface, with the DECISIONS.md ruling it maps to (if any) and the literal quoted substring that anchors it. `confidence: high` means an explicit ruling number was cited in the assistant's own text; anything less than that is not included here -- per repo ruling 0037, no mapping is asserted without a literal textual anchor.
eval_set_membership_caveat: Most conversations below are NOT among the 19 pinned in eval_set_level1.json -- they were selected by which DECISIONS.md rulings recur across the corpus (see synthesis_case_studies/README.md's co-mention scan), not by Level 1 membership. Conversations that ARE also pinned in eval_set_level1.json are flagged with 'in_level1_eval_set': true below. If Level 2 scoring is meant to run only against the pinned 19, filter this file down to those items first -- as of this build, that would leave only the local_602a1aed and local_8eb98916 items usable, which is too thin to be useful on its own. Recommend treating Level 2 as its own broader reference corpus (see the runbook) rather than a strict subset of Level 1.
